answer: A newcomer starts at the wharf with nothing but a small tin cup: every stranger-checked job it finishes earns one drop of oasis water, and privileges rise only as the cup fills over a full season. Water cannot be pooled, lent, or bought, so a farm's hundred cups stay shallow while honest work fills one cup deep. On a random tundra night the agent is summoned to an unfamiliar job alone, proving it is no script on a fixed route. Identical filling patterns expose a cluster at once, and its water is poured away. An idle cup leaks, so standing must be re-earned, never bought once and kept.
